title: docs(objectql): Multi-Tenant Schemas says the injected organization_id is stamped on insert and NOT NULL on a table the driver creates
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DPad2G8LxwxKbL6HrM92a5Z)_

Fixes #25137

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changed

One file, docs only: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/schema.mdx`, section "Multi-Tenant Schemas" (+19 / -3).

- The parenthetical that said the injected `organization_id` "is server-populated on insert and stays NULL where no organization context exists" now says the platform stamps it on insert, so the author never writes it.
- A new paragraph after the first YAML example says what `main` does, each claim with its source:
  - `required: false` is the authoring surface, not the stored value; NULL is not an organization (ADR-0131 D1).
  - An insert is stamped with the writer's organization, under `single` with the Default Organization, and a write that names none is refused wherever an organization can exist (ADR-0131 D9).
  - A table the SQL or Turso driver creates carries the column `NOT NULL` at `CREATE TABLE`, so the database refuses a row with no organization, an `upsert` included (ADR-0131 D1's driver note, and the `tenant-column-not-null-ddl` changeset of `@objectstack/driver-sql` / `@objectstack/driver-turso`). The in-memory driver enforces no `NOT NULL` (the same D1 note).
  - A table that already existed keeps a nullable column until `os migrate organization-ownership` tightens it; the ceremony cannot tighten a rotated shard or a Turso remote table; `os migrate plan` lists every tenant column still nullable (the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet; ADR-0131 D1 and its 2026-10-22 amendment, item 2). Both are linked to their `deployment/cli` sections.
  - An object whose rows belong to no organization opts out and has no column (the changeset's remedy; ADR-0131 D1). The opt-out paragraph that already follows is unchanged.

**D1's wording, measured before citing it.** The card and the changeset both quote D1 as "There is no nullable tenant column anywhere". That sentence is no longer D1: the 2026-10-22 amendment (ruling of record `6328195425`) replaced it with a paragraph that says where the column is NOT NULL and which nullable columns remain. So the page cites D1 for what the amended text says (NOT NULL at the engine and at every table the driver creates; NULL is not a state), and does not quote the retired sentence.

## Per-hit verdicts (the other pages)

- **A3 (#25135 not found open)**: holds, with the reason: #25135 merged on 2026-10-21T20:45Z. It corrected the same sentence in three code comments (`registry.ts`, `registry-tenant-index-declaration.test.ts`, `object.zod.ts`) and named this page under its Acceptance notes, carrier none. ## Acceptance notes

- `seed-tenancy-repair.mdx` describes its defect in the present tense (`:30-34`, and `:72` "At `kernel:ready` on a fresh install no organization exists yet"). On `main` the `single` posture creates the Default Organization at boot, before seeds load, and the seed loader refuses an organization-less row on an install that registers the organization object (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`, the `unowned` branch). The section is anchored to 17.0.0 GA, so this PR leaves it; a reader on 18.x may still take it for today's behaviour. Carrier: none.
- The page cites the changeset by its name, not its path: a release consumes `.changeset/*.md`, and the sentence then lives in the two drivers' `CHANGELOG.md`. ADR-0131 D1's driver note carries the same fact durably.
- The attribution block's first line is an HTML comment the session requires as the body's first line; `os-dev.md` forbids HTML comments in GitHub text. It is the same shape PR #25255 carried through the relay; reported as a deviation.
